subject: Multi-year tranche proposal + burst bridge for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena.p@NimbusLabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@nimbuslabs.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal conversation — multi-year with burst need

Hi Grace,

As we discussed on last week’s call, Nimbus is planning to expand usage materially over the next 18 months. A few specifics from procurement/finance: 

- We prefer a multi-year commitment (24 months) with a front-loaded burst allowance for Q1/Q2 next year (expected temporary usage spike ~2.5x baseline).
- We'd like the option to purchase additional burst capacity by the quarter rather than renegotiating the term.
- Finance is asking for an option to split invoicing: annual invoice for committed capacity + quarterly pass-through for burst overages (can be invoiced separately).

Can you share a proposal or term sheet we can review with our legal team? Also copy in your pricing contact so we can get a ballpark.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Petrova
Head of Cloud Ops, Nimbus Labs
elena.p@nimbuslabs.com

Attachments: none
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.p@NimbusLabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — multi-year with burst need

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear priorities.

We can absolutely support the structure you outlined. High-level we propose: 

- 24-month committed tranche (baseline committed GPUs/slots) priced with a graduated discount schedule at year 2.
- A separate "burst bridge" pool available in Q1/Q2 next year sized to cover the 2.5x spike; burst is metered and billed quarterly.
- Quarterly overage invoices for burst; annual invoice for committed tranche (we can supply split-invoice format).
- An optional top-up purchase window each quarter (holds pricing for 30 days) so you don't have to re-contract.

I’m attaching a draft term sheet and a capacity schedule (spreadsheet) that lays out an example ramp and how billing would flow. Marcus/Monica — could you validate the pricing bands and confirm whether we can offer a 6% additional discount if Nimbus commits to a 36-month renewal trigger at the end of year two?

If this looks reasonable, Elena — I can send a clean term sheet with the DocuSign link for legal to review.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
(Attachment: NIM-2028_term_tranche_v1.pdf (pdf); NIM-2028_capacity_burst_schedule.xlsx (xlsx))
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 09:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — multi-year with burst need

Grace — quick internal notes and numbers (replying inline for context).

> We can absolutely support the structure you outlined. High-level we propose:
> - 24-month committed tranche (baseline committed GPUs/slots) priced with a graduated discount schedule at year 2.
> - A separate "burst bridge" pool available in Q1/Q2 next year sized to cover the 2.5x spike; burst is metered and billed quarterly.

Sounds good. Pricing guardrails:
- Baseline committed tier priced per-token equivalent (we'll map their slot count to tokens after sizing call).
- Burst metering should have a floor price and a volume cap per quarter so finance isn't surprised. Recommend setting a per-quarter soft cap with notification at 75% burn.

> Marcus/Monica — could you validate the pricing bands and confirm whether we can offer a 6% additional discount if Nimbus commits to a 36-month renewal trigger at the end of year two?

Yes on validating bands. On the 36-month trigger discount: we can offer a conditional 6% if (a) they sign initial 24-month, (b) provide a Letter of Intent to convert to 36 after 18 months, and (c) accept standard auto-renew with a 60-day opt-out. Need legal to confirm the exact clause language.

Operational notes for onboarding/ops:
- Monica: we will need a kickoff >60 days before the Q1 ramp to validate KV cache sizing and pre-warm strategies.
- Jonas: confirm burst pool allocation mechanics — whether it’s separate allocation or a soft overlay on existing workers.

I’ll put a pricing spreadsheet update in the attachments for Grace to send along.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(Attachment: pricing_bands_NIM-2028.xlsx (xlsx))
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Petrova <elena.p@NimbusLabs.com>, Contracts <contracts@nimbuslabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 15:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Final term sheet and next steps (NIM-2028-42)

Elena / Contracts team — attaching the revised term sheet that incorporates the tranche + burst bridge language and the split-invoice approach your finance team requested. Summary of changes from the draft: 

- Committed tranche: 24 months, baseline capacity as defined in the capacity schedule. Automatic pricing step-down of 3% on month 13; conditional 6% end-of-year-two conversion discount if Nimbus confirms a 36-month extension by month 18 (LOI accepted).
- Burst bridge: metered quarterly billing; soft cap per quarter with automated alerts at 75% consumption. Separate quarterly invoice for burst consumption.
- Billing: annual invoice for committed tranche (Net 30), quarterly invoices for burst usage (Net 30). We can produce consolidated statements on request.
- Operational: 60+ day onboarding window before Q1 ramp; pre-warm and KV-cache validation included as part of onboarding.

Attachments: final term sheet and capacity schedule. Please route to legal and let us know any redlines. If this matches your internal goals I will send the DocuSign link and assign the HubSpot deal to "Commitment pending signature".

Next steps I propose: 
1) Contracts review (Nimbus legal) — target return with redlines in 5 business days.
2) Tech kickoff scheduled for week-of Oct 8 (aligned to 60-day pre-warm).
3) DocuSign sent on approval — we will aim for an executed agreement by Sep 8 to hit onboarding timelines.

Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
